rule: adjusted_score desc, total_score desc; dedupe by arXiv id / URL / id / title

papers.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
papers.authors: Pan Zhang, Nan Zhuang, Yongkang Zhang, Kun Xú, Zhongtao Jiang, Zhiwei Wang, Kun Xǔ, Youhuan Li
papers.summary: Continuous generative retrievers sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel ANN search, yet independent queries often land in overlapping neighborhoods and waste a fixed budget on duplicate items. CACO attaches a lightweight adjustment network to frozen flow-matching and diffusion backbones, using user history and inter-query interaction to adjust query positions. It uses item retrieval frequency across a reference query pool as a label-free relevance weight where duplicates add no gain. During self-supervised training, it holds other queries fixed and compares opposite perturbations for marginal coverage gain to bypass non-differentiable ANN search. ==Coordinating query positions under a fixed budget improves complementary coverage without changing the backbone or search depth.== Across eight public benchmarks and an in-house streaming industrial dataset, it raises Recall@400 by up to 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by more than half, adds at most 3.0% inference latency, and works plug-and-play across six frozen backbones.

papers.title: LQ-Rec: Late Quantization for Sequential Recommendation
papers.authors: Satoshi Koide, Yueqi Wang, Julian McAuley
papers.summary: Autoregressive generative recommendation with Semantic IDs faces a structural scaling limit, because longer codes reduce quantization error in principle yet make prediction harder, often degrading ranking quality while inflating encoder memory and decoding cost. LQ-Rec moves quantization to the candidate item side while keeping the sequence encoder and inner-product scoring in continuous space, jointly training the encoder and residual quantizer before freezing the encoder to fine-tune the codebook across every prefix length. ==Because the user vector never reads discrete tokens, model error and quantization error separate additively==, so ranking quality improves monotonically with code length. Across four public benchmarks, it outperforms the non-autoregressive baseline RPG by 19% to 57% in Recall@10 and leads existing Semantic ID baselines on unseen item transitions. At inference time, each query runs the encoder only once, and a single checkpoint can be truncated to shorter prefixes to trade off ranking quality and inference cost without retraining.

papers.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
papers.authors: Chen Qiu, Zhigang Hua, Qi Xu, Jizhe Zhang, Sha Hua, Ren Mao, Luke Simon
papers.summary: Items on a recommendation page compete for attention and complement one another, so placing the individually best candidates side by side rarely yields the best page. Existing generative re-ranking either assigns one page-level score to every choice, or fits fixed target lists built before training that stop adapting as the generator improves. Given a fixed evaluator, Meta trains the generator in rounds: at each partial page, it places candidates next, lets the current model sample completions, scores each full page, and reweights probabilities into per-position cross-entropy targets. The updated model then builds the next round's data. ==Each position adjusts candidate distributions using complete-page scores==, so serving runs greedy decoding without evaluator search. Under offline referee evaluation on KuaiRand-1K, RL4RS-SeqSlate, and industrial feed logs, it outperforms the evaluated generative recommendation and RL baselines as well as prefix-score beam search, lifting industrial page scores by 13.92% over logged pages compared with the strongest baseline DeGRe at 12.75%. On a synthetic benchmark with known optima, it reaches 97.16% of the optimal score, with its lead coming from page-context contributions.

papers.title: Generative News Recommendation Reproduces Popularity: A Memorization-Based Analysis
papers.authors: Shotaro Ishihara
papers.summary: When a large language model recommends news by generating article titles directly, its outputs become more concentrated than users' actual browsing logs, and training-data memorization is one mechanism behind this concentration. Using about 20 million browsing sessions from the Japanese news service Nikkei Online, the author continually trained an instruction-tuned Llama 3 8B model to predict the next title. It generated only 20,689 distinct titles, roughly one-fifth of the observed next-title types, with higher concentration and lower diversity. Correlation analysis shows that frequently repeated target titles exhibit stronger verbatim and approximate memorization, and more strongly memorized titles are generated across more prompts. An exploratory target-level deduplication condition lowered memorization and concentration while nearly doubling distinct generated titles, but shrank the training data to about one-hundredth of its size, sharply cut exact-match accuracy, and did not improve semantic diversity. To curb popularity concentration in production without indiscriminate deduplication, the author suggests combining frequency-aware loss reweighting with recency decay, candidate-constrained decoding, and diversity-aware reranking.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
papers.authors: Chang Yang, Yao Xuan, Wendan Yan, Nhat Le, Jiang Liu, Longhao Jin, Zhen Peggy Yao, Alireza Vahdatpour, Djordje Gligorije...
papers.summary: Large web platforms run fleets of ads ranking models, and inheriting old features with manual edits struggles to balance per-model serving costs against shared feature pipeline budgets. Meta built a fleet-scale system where LLM agents propose hypotheses and deterministic tools run and verify experiments, finding that ==gains usually come from rebalancing volume across feature categories, since scaling every category up hits diminishing returns==. A shared retrieval LLM, continually fine-tuned on outcomes across the fleet, shortlists cross features before deterministic importance estimators and multi-task Pareto fronts blend the rankings, and a search agent then runs asynchronous trials under serving resource caps. Before training, a trimming step swaps over-budget additions for already-used features of the same category under the same budget. Across production models, it improves NE by 0.31% on average within each model’s budget, trimming cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% on average with no regression beyond measurement noise, and launched models lift a primary online metric by 0.20% in A/B tests.

papers.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
papers.authors: Anish Khazane, Alex Saad-Falcon, Guanchu Wu, Marcio Porto, Jasper Shan, Fei Yu, Eugene Shulga, Intaik Park, Yongzhe Zhan...
papers.summary: When training large-scale recommendation models, GPU count is often constrained not by compute, but by sparse embedding tables filling up HBM. Existing in-training embedding pruning (ITEP) dynamically drops less important rows during training, yet usually sets pruning ratios by table size, ignoring feature contributions and sometimes hurting accuracy. Meta's FI-ITEP instead precomputes feature importance, such as by shuffling a feature's values within a batch and measuring the loss change, then assigns higher pruning ratios to less important tables. Across three industry-scale recommendation models, it cuts total memory by 20% to 40% while matching or beating size-based pruning in accuracy, and the same trend holds on the open-source DLRM benchmark. The freed memory lets a frequently retrained model drop from 112 to 80 GPUs with higher per-GPU throughput. ==Larger models carry more low-contribution embeddings, so the compute saved outweighs the upfront estimation cost==; for smaller models with less redundancy, size-based pruning may suffice.

papers.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation
papers.authors: Zhixiong Hu, Meng Li, Maggie Zhang, Deborshi Goswami, David Bailey, James Bradley
papers.summary: Autodesk recommends product pages, industry pages, customer stories, and learning content on one site, where standard item-ID sequence encoders drop web events without catalog IDs and running an LLM synchronously breaks latency budgets. LSER keeps the existing two-tower model and sequence encoder, using a fine-tuned LLM to turn raw event text into auxiliary session and history embeddings inside the user tower. Heavy encoding runs asynchronously in a nearline pipeline into an embedding store, so live requests read the stored vectors for ANN search. In offline ablation, adding these LLM features raises popular-product HR@10 by 9.6 percentage points and customer-story HR@1 by 6.0 percentage points, while other surfaces stay essentially flat. The completed online A/B test compared the nearline two-tower stack without the LLM features against the legacy rule engine, lifting product order submission rate by 14.8%, with live testing of the LLM features planned next. ==For sparse multi-content sites, refreshing raw-event LLM features nearline adds semantic signal within retrieval latency limits.==

papers.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
papers.authors: Ben Kang, Junda Wang, Yuxuan Yuan, Hang Li, Yuhan Liu, Xin Chen, Wanting Geng, Tong Lin, Pei Fu, Dong Wang, Jian Luan, H...
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models understand multimodal inputs and task instructions well, yet compressing an input into a single embedding vector does not ensure preserving fine-grained clues such as color or spatial relations to separate relevant items from confusable distractors. The two-stage framework DiLE first guides a few learnable latent queries with a reasoning instruction, combining shared and task-private LoRA experts with auxiliary answer-generation supervision. Stage two periodically refreshes hard negatives retrieved by updated student snapshots and aligns embedding similarities with a frozen reranker teacher distribution via reverse KL divergence. ==At inference, each input is encoded in a single pass into precomputable vectors without the teacher or explicit reasoning traces.== Across configurations spanning two backbone generations, DiLE achieves state-of-the-art overall performance on MMEB-V2, MRMR, and UVRB. With Qwen3-VL-2B on MMEB-V2, it outperforms Embed-RL on the same backbone by 2.8% while running 101x faster.

papers.title: 4 modalities, 100+ languages, 1 vector space: Jina Embeddings v5 in Microsoft Foundry
papers.summary: A single search query can return both a video clip and a text paragraph in the same result set. Jina Embeddings v5 is now in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog with four models across text and Omni multimodal families: the Omni models map text, images, PDFs, audio, and video into one vector space, while the text models cover over 100 languages. Both families come in Small and Nano sizes, with Small offering more parameters and a longer context window for accuracy and Nano targeting throughput. On the MMTEB multilingual text benchmark, Nano gives up about 1.5 points to Small while processing text 3.4x faster, ties Small on audio while running faster, and trails Small clearly on images and video. Models run as dedicated endpoints in your own Azure subscription, billed by compute hour, keeping models and data inside the tenant with vectors going straight into Elasticsearch. Because catalog deployments block outbound access, multimodal inputs must be passed as Base64 rather than media URLs.

papers.title: SAGE: Semantic Ambiguity Guided Capacity Expansion for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.authors: Xunlei Chen, Jinyu Guo, Yi Gong, Qirui Ye, Zhaokun Wang, Wenyi Li, Wenhong Tian
papers.summary: Structure-augmented RAG methods improve multi-hop reasoning, yet they incur high indexing costs and degrade on simple queries. The authors argue this robustness gap stems from capacity bottlenecks in fixed-dimensional inner-product scoring. As corpora grow, semantically close passages form local regions where a base scorer cannot maintain sufficient separability. ==Reorganizing documents into trees or graphs can expose or partially mitigate this issue, yet it does not by itself provide a stronger local scoring function.== The lightweight RAG framework SAGE detects these regions using document-side Local Separability Deficit and expands capacity only where needed. It builds a two-layer semantic index, derives atomic query views from corpus passages, and calibrates a parameter-efficient hypernetwork to generate local Ambiguity-Conditioned Scorers for selected nodes. Extensive experiments show that SAGE improves retrieval and QA performance over dense retrievers and structure-augmented baselines, achieving a better balance between single-hop and multi-hop retrieval accuracy and robust scalability.

papers.title: Iterate Until Retrieved: Factual Nugget Optimization for Discoverable Continual Corrections in Agentic RAG
papers.authors: Moshe Hazoom, Gal Patel, Alon Talmor, Tom Hope
papers.summary: Agentic RAG systems in B2B settings often receive free-form response feedback, and rather than generic signals such as style, preference, or overall response quality, the authors focus on actionable factual corrections, identifying and converting them into compact knowledge-base entries called factual nuggets. They introduce Iterative Nugget Optimization (INO), an index-time optimization method that uses the production agentic RAG system as a test harness. INO creates an initial nugget, probes it with the triggering query and paraphrases, reflects over failed retrieval and answer traces, and revises the nugget until it is discoverable. Evaluation covers two production B2B knowledge-assistance agents across multiple companies that use the system: a product support agent answering over company-specific knowledge bases, and a support ticket agent assisting support engineers. Across automated and human evaluations, INO consistently improves discoverability and usage of factual corrections over baselines, and a controlled production experiment shows that the nuggets improve user satisfaction with responses.

papers.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
papers.authors: Jiatong Ma, Yuchen Liu, Longteng Guo, Yichen Yuan, Yuze Wu, Dongze Hao, Ru Zhen, Yanhao Zhang, Haonan Lu, Jing Liu
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models still struggle with vision-centric knowledge questions, where the strongest model reaches only 57.1% overall accuracy without external knowledge yet exceeds 90% once gold evidence is provided. Earlier benchmarks mostly use the input image only to identify an entity and then rely on text-based knowledge. VC-VQA pairs a controlled Wikipedia snapshot of traceable textual and visual evidence with three tasks covering pre-retrieval image clues, post-retrieval image verification, and external image evidence. Giving models the ground-truth entity names lifts internal visual reasoning by about 39% but raises external visual reasoning by only about 1%, showing that models recall textual attributes once an entity is named while fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition remains the main bottleneck. ==Multi-step agentic retrieval outperforms single-step heuristic retrieval across all evaluated models==, pointing to the need for iterative planning and coordinated visual and textual retrieval.

papers.title: TableRoute: Capability-Aware Routing for Scalable Table Question Answering
papers.authors: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi
papers.summary: Using one fixed inference strategy for LLM table question answering breaks down across short, long, and massive tables. Error sampling shows that semantic mismatches linking questions to the wrong columns or values rank first across all scales at 42.3% of failures, while a model's reliable table-length limit is much lower for aggregation and arithmetic than for simple lookup. TableRoute first extracts column, value, and condition evidence from a compact table profile, verifies its executability, and identifies the required operations. ==It then selects a single route from table length and offline-calibrated capability limits==, running only direct reading, table reduction, or program execution while reusing that evidence. Across three benchmarks covering all three scales, it outperforms the strongest baseline on all three base models; on massive-table BirdQA, average accuracy improves by 5.3 points while online cost drops from 160.4K tokens per question for multi-agent TALON to 24.6K. Each new base model requires a one-time offline calibration.

papers.title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
papers.authors: Francisco W. Kerche, Franziska Sofia Hafner, Felix M. Simon, Luc Rocher
papers.summary: When users in Latin America turn to web-enabled language models for news, the sources they see are generally less diverse, and local users get fewer domestic outlets than from conventional search engines. A University of Oxford team compiled over 1,900 recent events across nine Latin American countries, varied user location and query language across four user scenarios, and compared three search engines against four language models. For local users searching from their own country in the local language, search engines already return only 41.3% domestic news, while the four language models return 3.6 to 11.6 percentage points less than the search-engine average, with inconsistent patterns across the other scenarios. Language models rely on a narrower pool of outlets overall, and all four trail search engines on within-country diversity for English queries. ==LLM-based search reproduces geographic biases from web search and can amplify them in some settings.== Evaluating web-grounded AI search therefore requires auditing source retrieval and selection across locations and languages alongside answer quality.

papers.title: LSP-RAG: Latent Scoring Perspectives for Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.authors: Haochen Liu, Guanghui Min, Song Wang, Yada Zhu, Chen Chen, Jundong Li
papers.summary: In multi-hop knowledge graph RAG, a frozen lightweight language model can outperform large models like ChatGPT as the retriever. Prior lightweight retrievers score candidate triplets from a single angle and in isolation, missing diverse relevance signals and often dropping relations that look weak alone yet connect earlier reasoning steps. LSP-RAG prepends two sets of trainable continuous prompts to a frozen lightweight language model. One set induces multiple latent scoring perspectives weighted adaptively by the question and candidate triplet, while the other aggregates prior-hop candidate representations to carry reasoning context across hops. On WebQSP, LSP-RAG with a Flan-T5-3B retriever reaches 88.59% accuracy, ahead of ChatGPT-guided RoG at 74.27%, and it also outperforms all compared baselines on WikiMovies and both single-hop and two-hop MetaQA. For RAG teams, ==multi-hop filtering over structured knowledge graphs can shift to a lightweight model, leaving the large LLM for final answer generation==.

papers.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
papers.authors: Yuhao Zhou, Yang Zhou, Yuanxi Li, Jindi Lv, Dan Si, Qing Ye, Jiancheng Lv
papers.summary: When small models run deep-research agents locally, single-pass selection is error-prone, while testing alternatives through real execution spends external tool calls on discarded branches. Seer separates action proposal from decision guidance: a frozen agent proposes candidate actions, while a tool-response simulator and a history value estimator are trained offline on real trajectories. Each round, the simulator predicts candidate tool outputs and the estimator scores the imagined histories, ==so only the selected action calls external tools while discarded branches use only local compute==, and committed histories keep only real responses. Without retraining any model, GAIA accuracy for Qwen3.5-4B rises from 13.6% to 41.7%, and the same checkpoints transfer to Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma-4, and larger models with real tool calls on BrowseComp-200 staying close to the base agent. Wider candidate search can offset simulation errors but amplifies scoring noise, so candidate width needs tuning per model and task.

papers.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
papers.authors: Meenakshi Rajpurohit, Anna Phan, Ravikumar Komandur Narayanan, Gunanidhi Ramakrishnan, Nathan Howland
papers.summary: Asking a single LLM to answer questions about SEC filings and stock prices often yields wrong ratios, stale prices, and confident routing errors. The open-source prototype FinVeriQA splits each job: the decision model Laya routes queries and blocks investment advice, Python computes every number, retrieval and live quotes fetch evidence, and Mistral-7B writes answers checked by code. This removes calculation and stale-price errors, yet in live tests two correctly routed answers still passed validation while reporting AMD sample data under NVIDIA's and Alphabet's names. The issue is that the validator reads the same shared evidence as the writer. In a controlled upper-bound study on FinRank, replacing one figure in the shared passage with a plausible wrong value leaves Mistral-7B's multi-sample agreement intact while accuracy drops to zero. A shared-evidence check catches only 35% of these errors, compared with 77% when checking against the uncorrupted original passage. For multi-agent QA and RAG systems, ==verification must be independent of the shared evidence the writer saw==, or corrupted figures and wrong-company data will slip through.

papers.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.authors: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han, Qinghao Hu
papers.summary: In hybrid LLMs, global-attention KV cache grows with both concurrency and context length, while bounded-state cache scales only with concurrency, so fixed GPU memory partitions can leave one pool underused while the other blocks requests. Hierarchical caching like HiCache keeps restored prefixes resident in GPU memory during decode, leaving the high-bandwidth CPU-GPU interconnect largely idle. Built in SGLang, TideCache keeps fixed virtual addresses for each cache subpool and remaps physical GPU pages on demand, shifting capacity across pools without changing cache layouts or attention backends. ==During decode, it uses bounded-state computation intervals to prefetch the next global-attention layer's host prefix into shared GPU slots==, keeping generated KV resident while the scheduler selects resident or streamed execution from request size and queue state. Across seven model and platform configurations on GB300 and GH200, it completes up to 2.04 times as many agent turns as SGLang with HiCache, cuts overall P50 per-token latency by 20% to 59%, and substantially improves agent P50 TTFT.

papers.title: Supercharging XLA-based inference: Announcing the launch of XLA Serving Engine
papers.authors: Oleg Shaldybin, Monica Song
papers.summary: Many teams train models in Python, yet some production environments disallow Python and face interpreter and global interpreter lock overhead, so Google has open-sourced XLA Serving Engine for the OpenXLA ecosystem. It exports JAX models to an XLA SavedModel storing StableHLO computations and Orbax weights, then runs them in a native C++ runtime wrapping PJRT and the XLA compiler, supporting single-host and multi-host serving while preserving training kernel optimizations. In Google's short-request studies, it achieves 2 to 5 times the throughput of the best Python server they could build using a quarter of the memory. Internally, it already serves over 6 million queries per second across YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, Search, and parts of Gemini Omni. ==It is built as a lightweight one-shot inference engine typically for non-LLM models==, while the authors recommend vLLM or SGLang for large autoregressive language models with long contexts, and PyTorch export via TorchTPU is planned.

papers.title: E2E: Efficient Filtered AKNN Search via Adaptive Termination
papers.authors: Wenxuan Xia, Mingyu Yang, Wentao Li, Wei Wang
papers.summary: In filtered approximate nearest neighbor search, graph indexes such as HNSW typically apply a fixed termination rule to every query, causing easy queries to explore far too many nodes. Early-termination models built for plain vector search look only at traversal distances and break down under filters, because ==when attributes and vector distances misalign, nearby nodes may still fail the filter==. During the mandatory early probing phase of graph search, E2E records the filter-matching ratios of visited nodes and queued candidates. It feeds both ratios and distance features into a lightweight LightGBM model to predict each query's computation budget, stopping easy queries early while letting hard ones search longer. In the high-recall regime, compared with Naive HNSW, it runs up to 2.6× faster on Tripclick and reduces distance computations by up to three times on YoutubeAudio, while improving efficiency by up to 1.5× when adapted to the filter-aware index ACORN. Without altering the underlying graph index, offline training on historical query logs cuts redundant traversal on easy filtered queries.

papers.title: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
papers.authors: Yingqi Shi, Junru Lu, Yun Liu, Di Yin, Xing Sun
papers.summary: In long-context block-sparse attention, giving every query a fixed block budget wastes work on weakly related blocks when scores are concentrated and drops relevant blocks when scores are diffuse. Assigning GPU work by query range also forces multiple thread blocks to reload the same KV block repeatedly. LightningMoBA keeps MoBA's mean-pooled block scoring and softmax computation, switching block selection to a per-query relative score threshold. It organizes execution around KV blocks, splits heavily selected blocks into row-capped subtasks, and uses Hopper GPU pipelining to overlap KV transfers, irregular query gathers, and matrix computation. Across five checkpoints on RULER at a matched Top-16 budget, it accelerates end-to-end generation by 1.20 to 1.60× over FlashMoBA. Mean RULER score rises from 74.42 to 75.28, though variable tracking drops across all five models at 64K context. Same-backend comparisons show execution optimizations drive most small-budget speedups, while at Top-64 dynamic routing yields simultaneous speed and accuracy gains on the evaluated models.

papers.title: Berth: SLO-Preserving GPU Sharing Without New Preemption
papers.authors: Mohammadali Khodabandehlou, Mahdi Alizadeh, Lei Gao, Murali Annavaram, Bhaskar Krishnamachari
papers.summary: Online inference GPUs sit largely idle off-peak, yet co-locating best-effort work such as training often breaks millisecond SLOs, and existing fixes either nearly halt the background job or rewrite kernels and patch drivers. This work shows that the stock time-slicer on commodity GPUs already preempts running kernels in under a millisecond; ==what it lacks is priority, which can be created in user space==. Berth is an unprivileged user-space system that leaves applications, frameworks, closed libraries, and drivers untouched. It holds best-effort kernel launches while a request is in flight, caps queued work during idle gaps, and shortens only the best-effort time slice to bound long kernels. Across MLPerf scenarios, Berth reaches 95.8% average SLO attainment, close to 97.9% alone, while keeping 48% of solo best-effort throughput, more than two and a half times what the closest baselines retain. For continuous-batching LLM serving, Berth feeds background work within each step's remaining slack, meeting per-token targets for nearly every request while training keeps running.

papers.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
papers.authors: Payman Behnam, Elaheh Sobhani, Saad Amin, Yahya Hassan, Daniyal Khan, Biswadeep Chakraborty, Tanish Patwa, Souvik Kundu,...
papers.summary: When large reasoning models generate long chains of thought, decode-stage KV cache compression depends heavily on timing. On AIME25, approximate attention token selection has little effect when output probabilities are concentrated, yet in uncertain steps with spread-out probabilities the flip rate of the most likely next token reaches 65%. Overly long generations with repetitive reasoning are also more likely to end in wrong answers. RoCoKV uses the entropy of the previous step's output distribution to adapt its budget without an extra forward pass, ==keeping more context during uncertain steps and pruning harder during confident ones==. It also uses a compact summary of recent context to down-weight repetitive tokens, avoiding full-cache pairwise comparisons. On the systems side, it plugs into vLLM with fused three-phase CUDA kernels that preserve paged KV cache management and CUDA graph execution, ==turning sparse compression into end-to-end speedups==. Across two reasoning models and three math benchmarks, it achieves higher accuracy than the evaluated compression baselines under tight budgets. Serving DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on AIME25 in vLLM, it delivers a 1.27x speedup and 38% higher throughput than Full-KV.

papers.title: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect -- KV Cache Management for AI Agents
papers.authors: Shashwat Jaiswal, Chloe Alverti, Mengmei Ye, Chen Wang, Hubertus Franke, Fan Lai, Tianyin Xu, Josep Torrellas
papers.summary: When multiple LLM agents run tool calls concurrently, idle KV cache blocks are quickly evicted from GPU memory and host DRAM, stalling returning requests for seconds on SSD reads. Pinning idle blocks in GPU memory or prefetching them straight to the GPU instead consumes scarce GPU capacity and lengthens queues. Because an agent's reused prefix is already known and only tool duration is uncertain, TripleKV predicts tool completion from tool type, input arguments, and live output cues, then prefetches the needed KV blocks from SSD into host DRAM. In DRAM, a multi-queue policy protects prefetched blocks from premature LRU eviction and removes duplicates of GPU-resident blocks. ==Prefetching into host DRAM instead of scarce GPU memory hides slow SSD reads without competing with active inference.== Across four agentic benchmarks, it cuts requests needing critical-path SSD reads from up to 76% to under 10%, lowers P95 TTFT by up to 49% over vLLM with DRAM and SSD tiers, and outperforms recent GPU-pinning and GPU-prefetching systems on tail latency and throughput.

papers.title: Twindex: Index Cache Offloading with Coarse-to-Fine Selection for Long-Context Sparse-Attention Serving
papers.authors: Yuxuan Xia, Jiakun Fan, Han Meng, Hao Mark Chen, Shenji Wan, Dongsheng Yang
papers.summary: During million-token decoding in sparse-attention models, even after offloading the main KV cache to host memory, the indexer cache left in GPU memory still caps concurrency, taking up to 90% of per-request HBM across the three tested Qwen, DeepSeek, and GLM models. Because the indexer scans every past entry at each step, direct PCIe offloading is too slow, while plain low-precision compression hurts recall. Twindex fits a shared cross-input position component offline and compresses only the residual, keeping compact keys and a hot buffer in HBM while storing full native rows in host memory. ==Each step screens a larger candidate set with compact keys, then rescores native rows with the original indexer for top-k==, without changing model weights and inside CUDA graphs. When host memory does not limit batch size and Qwen and GLM share prefix main KV, decode throughput across the three models reaches 1.25 to 2.54 times an optimized main-KV-offloading baseline, with mean benchmark scores at most 3.1% below baseline. Once the index shrinks, host memory can become the next concurrency bottleneck.

papers.title: Announcing distributed KV caching for self-hosted LLMs with Amazon ElastiCache
papers.authors: Meet Bhagdev, Chaitanya Nuthalapati, Kevin McGehee
papers.summary: When self-hosted LLM inference serves long-context multi-turn chats or document Q&A, single-server GPU and host memory KV caches are capacity-limited and local to one host, forcing prefill recomputation when requests route elsewhere, sessions return later, or a node fails. Amazon has launched fully managed distributed KV caching on ElastiCache for Valkey, adding a shared cache tier across GPUs in the same Availability Zone. Engines including vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM connect via the open-source LMCache connector with only a configuration change, keeping hot blocks in DRAM, tiering colder blocks to local NVMe, and transferring KV state to GPU hosts via RDMA over EFA. ==Sharing KV state across servers frees fleets from pinning requests to one host and lets scaled-out or surviving servers reuse cached prefixes.== In shared-document Q&A tests, per-server requests per second doubled and cost per million output tokens dropped 40% after paying for the cache node. Across eight models, cache hits cut TTFT by 55% to 93%. Long-context reuse and retail or ads workloads with shared system prompts gain the most, and teams can run open-source KVTrace offline to estimate savings first.

papers.title: ECHO-2: A Large-Scale Distributed Rollout Framework for Cost-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Jingwei Song, Meng Chen, Jie Xiao, Qingnan Ren, Jiaqi Huang, Yangshen Deng, Chris Tong, Wanyi Chen, Suli Wang, Zhisheng ...
papers.summary: During LLM RL post-training, rollout generation takes up most of the time, yet it usually shares expensive data-center GPUs with updates and often leaves the learner idle. ECHO-2 keeps centralized training on a small set of data-center GPUs and offloads rollouts to cheaper heterogeneous inference workers over a wide-area network. It treats policy staleness as a controllable budget so rollout generation, weight broadcast, and training overlap, activating the lowest-cost workers per unit throughput needed to saturate the learner. During broadcasts, workers form parallel peer-forwarding chains that relay chunks and switch to the new snapshot once installed, relieving the learner uplink bottleneck. In GRPO math post-training on Qwen3-8B over a wide-area network, it cuts cumulative cost by 33.3% to 36.3% over centralized baselines at matched AIME accuracy, with quality staying close to the synchronous baseline up to 6 steps of staleness. ==With bounded staleness and peer-forwarded broadcasts absorbing wide-area latency, cheaper distributed inference can take over rollout workloads without stalling training.==
